clue.text: Send off letters that may appear under one's name

definitions.text: that may appear under one's name

parts.note: to send off a letter is to post it
script is handwriting, a set of written letters

explanation.surface: Someone dispatching correspondence that carries their signature at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterthought added after a letter's signature sits below the writer's name.

clue.text: Notice a sort of light pastry

definitions.meaning: a flattering review or write-up, a notice in the press
... pastry is a flaky, airy kind

explanation.definitionFit: A favourable press mention is a puff, and flaky layered pastry is called puff pastry.

clue.text: A cleaner programme?

definitions.meaning: a serial drama on television or radio

explanation.surface: Asking whether some show is a cleaner one than another.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing bar cleans, and a long-running domestic drama serial is known as a soap opera.

clue.text: Burns classification is postgraduate's objective

definitions.meaning: burns are graded by depth, first, second and third
a postgraduate works toward a master's, a further qualification after the first

explanation.surface: Claims that a scale for injuries is what a graduate student aims for.
explanation.definitionFit: Medium-severity burns are graded at that level, and a master's is a further university qualification.

clue.text: Bra is expected to offer uplift

indicators.note: the words Bra is expected offer up, inside them, a run of letters

explanation.surface: Underwear is supposed to give support.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across bRA IS Expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To uplift something is to lift or elevate it, a synonym.

clue.text: Having advance knowledge sent price tumbling

indicators.note: tumbling means the letters of sent price fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A forecaster saw costs drop before they did.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight: someone with foreknowledge of events is said to be farsighted in this way.

clue.text: Stuff rejected as basis for brandy

indicators.note: rejected here means thrown back, so the word for stuff runs backwards

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Material cast aside as the starting point for a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns CRAM round. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grape pulp left after pressing is distilled into a brandy of the same name.

clue.text: Bill a state cut by half for a university

parts.note: AC, short for account, a bill

indicators.note: cut by means the first pieces are split open by the next

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation of California, a US state
demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: An invoice for a region halved, sent to a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a university' is adjectival: academical dress is what is worn at a university. 'cut by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to a college, as in robes worn at one.

clue.text: Rustics Antony asked for a loan?

definitions.meaning: people who live in rural areas
Mark Antony's speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar opens 'Friends, Romans, ... lend me your ears'

explanation.surface: Country folk whom Mark Antony tapped for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural dwellers are called by this name, and Antony addresses them in his famous oration asking them to lend ears.

clue.text: Prerogatives of father — Aeneas's

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
Aeneas's father, the word father carrying over, is Anchises in Virgil's Aeneid

explanation.surface: The privileges of a parent, namely the Trojan hero's.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash invites reading 'father' again: Aeneas's father was Anchises, whom he carried out of burning Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rights or privileges granted, such as the vote, are known by this word.

clue.text: Sort of ballads acceptable for Hindu gentleman

parts.note: W. S. Gilbert's comic verses are the Bab Ballads
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Folk songs fit for an Indian gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: In India the title is a respectful address, like Mister, for a gentleman.

clue.text: Abstracted what's second-hand?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., owned before by someone else

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes a thing used.
explanation.definitionFit: Preoccupied people are said to be so taken up, and a used item was owned earlier.

clue.text: Neath operative's unexpressed emotion

parts.note: neath is a poetic form of beneath, under
operative means in force, current

explanation.surface: A worker from the Welsh town Neath feeling something unspoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath looks like the town in South Wales but is the poetic word for beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden feeling running beneath the surface is described by this flow metaphor.

clue.text: Nasty housework -one's going, at last, to get stuck in

indicators.note: to get stuck in means to be pushed inside the chore

parts.note: dusting is a household chore
one is, I'S, gives IS

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word going

explanation.surface: Dreadful chores: someone eventually going to get stuck into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get stuck in' places the inserted letters straight after the chore's opening D.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting or horrid things are described with this adjective, a synonym.

clue.text: Turn to account I see, that's unfinished

parts.note: the I as printed is a capital letter I

indicators.note: unfinished means the word see loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Exploiting something, I gather, before it is complete.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in the clue is literally a capital I, giving CAPITAL I. 'unfinished' cuts SEE to SE; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something for profit is to use it to advantage, a synonym.

clue.text: Jumping bail — due in, but not available for hearing

indicators.note: jumping means the letters of the fodder leap into a new order

explanation.surface: A defendant who skips bail and is due in court cannot be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounds too faint to be heard are described as such, a synonym.

clue.text: Cold tea served in far from exciting orgy

indicators.note: served in means placed inside the next phrase's word

parts.note: banal means dull, far from exciting
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
char or cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Chilly tea offered at a dreary party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' signals the insertion; CHA (or char) is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken revel, named after Bacchus the god of wine, is an orgy.

clue.text: Work steadily to grasp popular historian

indicators.note: to grasp means the first word holds the next inside

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it steadily
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Toil diligently to understand a well-liked chronicler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grasp' signals the insertion. Pliny the Elder wrote a Roman Natural History.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliny the Elder was a Roman author of a vast encyclopedic natural history.

clue.text: Seeing state of course, enter gelding

parts.note: to go in is to enter
G is the abbreviation for gelding in racing form

explanation.surface: Checking the racecourse conditions before entering a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing the condition of the turf (firm, soft) is the course's going. 'Seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing reports describe ground conditions, such as soft or heavy, under this heading.

clue.text: Italian given extremely cosy home, say — in old Venice, for example

indicators.note: given a home means the Italian piece is housed inside
extremely means the first and last letters of the word cosy

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in gin and It
to say is to state

explanation.surface: An Italian finding a snug house in historic Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given ... home' signals the insertion, with 'given' a link. 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic Venice was an independent republic, a sovereign urban polity.

clue.text: One who transports reptiles from Asia?

definitions.text: One who transports reptiles from Asia?

parts.words: One who transports reptiles from Asia?
parts.note: transports reads as ships but means enchants: an Indian entertainer who mesmerises serpents with a pipe

explanation.definitionFit: Street performers in India hypnotise cobras with music, enrapturing the serpents.

clue.text: Disorder in city street is upsetting

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian city

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the street abbreviation goes backwards

explanation.surface: Trouble in a town where a road is in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns ST into TS. 'in' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Outbreaks of violent public unrest, plural, amount to civil disorder.

clue.text: Order a tub

definitions.meaning: the Most Honourable Order of the ..., a British order of chivalry

explanation.definitionFit: A British chivalric honour bears the name, and a washing tub shares it.

clue.text: Finish second best

parts.note: top means best, foremost

explanation.definitionFit: To halt or end something is a synonym for finishing it.

clue.text: One member of family in the academic stream

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A relative enrolled in a scholarly track.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames flowing through Oxford is called by this name. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's stretch of the Thames bears a goddess's name, a river by a university.

clue.text: Uncertain of moment to put in vote against

indicators.note: to put in means the next phrase's word is placed inside

parts.note: an instant is a moment
con is a vote against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Not sure whether this is the time to register opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put in' signals the insertion. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fickle or changeable things are unreliable, hence uncertain.

clue.text: Highlander's blow on the ear?

indicators.note: on the ear means as heard when spoken

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind, a blow

explanation.surface: A Scot cuffed about the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gaelic-speaking Scot from the north is a Celt of that name.

clue.text: Firm policy that all men should be brothers

definitions.text: Firm policy that all men should be brothers

parts.words: Firm policy that all men should be brothers
parts.note: firm means company; brothers means fellow trade unionists, so the whole workforce must be in the union

explanation.definitionFit: A workplace rule requiring union membership of every employee is this arrangement.
